# Klarna-grundaren vattnar ogräset

**Feed**: kort-och-lang  
**Published**: 2026-09-11  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

Kort och lång (DI) hosts Robert Andersson and Ulf Pettersson discuss a nervous market ahead of US CPI data. US 10-year yields are near 5%, oil is at $107 and markets expect ECB, Riksbanken and Fed rate hikes, while Trump's $5,000 handout pledge adds to fiscal worries. They cover Asker Healthcare's 20% drop after a Carnegie target-price cut, Hemnet stopping its buybacks, Rusta's weak organic growth, which sectors win or lose in the Swedish election (Studsvik, banks, construction/JM), Swedish small caps lagging on earnings revisions, Flat Capital's CEO exit, and Yubico as an AI-security play. Both expect a modest bounce in the Stockholm exchange next week.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 ASKER — Asker Healthcare | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Ulf is long after the 20% drop from Carnegie's target-price cut. He says it is too cheap and that the cash flow statement doesn't lie.

#### Reasoning

Host Ulf likes the niche: a serial acquirer of medtech consumables with many acquisition targets in Europe, scale advantages in procurement, and growth with good profitability. Carnegie's criticism of how the company capitalises investments and books revenue can be checked in the cash flow statement. He has not yet read the full Carnegie note, so the view is conditional. Co-host Robert disagrees: he stays away and thinks Asker is not as high quality as Addlife.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Carnegie's full analysis reveals further accounting issues
- if cash flow conversion deteriorates
- if acquisition-driven growth stalls

> *"Jag är lång, men med det förbehållet."*

---

### ⛔ HEM — Hemnet | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Robert is short: the early buyback halt sends a strong negative signal, prices are reportedly being cut and competition is rising.

#### Reasoning

Host Robert: stopping the buyback is a strong negative signal from the board. The new pay-after-sale model creates negative working capital. Reported price cuts hit the only driver of revenue growth. Competitors such as Booli and Boneo are gaining. Co-host Ulf takes the opposite view and would make a small dip buy after the roughly 20% fall, because he thinks the new customer-aligned payment model is the right strategy.

#### Sell Triggers

- if price increases resume
- if upcoming reports show stable revenue growth
- if competition from Booli/Boneo fades

> *"Men med Hemnet – absolut inte."*

---

### 🟠 SVIK — Studsvik | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 40%

Election-dependent nuclear play: Ulf would own it under a right-leaning government, not under a red-green one. Already expensive.

#### Reasoning

Host Ulf treats Studsvik as an election-sensitive stock. Its nuclear business depends on continued political support. A right-leaning win would make it worth owning despite the rich valuation; a red-green win would make it a stock to avoid. The election is on Sunday, so the view is short-term and binary.

#### Sell Triggers

- if a red-green government wins the election
- if nuclear policy support is withdrawn

> *"Blir det rödgrönt vill jag inte äga den där. Blir det blått skulle jag gärna äga den, även om den är dyr."*

---

### 🟠 JM — JM | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 45%

All parties pushed building subsidies in the final debate. JM's half-year report showed early signs of a housing recovery.

#### Reasoning

Host Robert sees construction as a winner whatever the election result, because every party promised subsidies to cut building costs, and construction has wide ripple effects. JM's CEO flagged a possible turn in housing starts. His caveat: subsidy-driven building while the population shrinks is a risk for house prices over time.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the subsidy promises are not enacted
- if housing starts fail to recover
- if rate hikes choke the housing market

> *"Om vi tänker JM, så kändes det ganska positivt igår."*

---

### 🟢 NEWA-B — New Wave | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Has fallen since its report and become cheap. Ulf thinks it can bottom out and grow even in a weak consumer market.

#### Reasoning

Host Ulf names New Wave as a small cap that has de-rated after a weak report. He argues a small company can still grow in a weak market and that the share may be bottoming. He admits the consumer environment is poor, so conviction is limited.

#### Sell Triggers

- if consumer demand weakens further
- if the next report shows continued sales decline

> *"Jag tycker att det känns som att New Wave kan bottna här på börsen."*

---

### ⛔ FLAT-B — Flat Capital | **AVOID** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 80%

CEO exit locks in an all-in Klarna strategy. It sold its AI winners to buy Klarna, is down 70% in a year and trades at a premium. Robert: buy Klarna directly instead.

#### Reasoning

Host Robert, the show's Flat expert, reads the CEO's resignation as a win for Siemiatkowski's push to concentrate on Klarna. That goes against the listing thesis of diversifying. He cites Peter Lynch's line about 'watering the weeds and cutting the flowers': Flat sold its AI holdings (OpenAI and others) and bought the laggard. With the stock at a premium to its holdings, he sees no reason to own it rather than Klarna itself.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Flat trades at a discount to its holdings
- if the strategy returns to diversified new investments

> *"Så jag ser ingen anledning att köpa den här aktien. Köp i så fall Klartina direkt på New York-börsen."*

---

### 🟢 YUBICO — Yubico | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

AI-driven hacking threats could boost demand for physical security keys. Strong list of blue-chip and tech customers, cost cuts done. Robert thinks the share may have bottomed.

#### Reasoning

Host Robert links Sam Altman's warnings about AI hacking to demand for hardware authentication that is harder for AI agents to break. Yubico's customers include the world's largest tech and AI companies. Past problems (erratic growth, high costs, weak communication) are being fixed through a savings programme. The upside case is YubiKey becoming a mass-market consumer product.

#### Sell Triggers

- if growth stays erratic
- if costs rise again
- if the consumer market for keys fails to develop

> *"Så jag ser det som att det här skulle kunna bli ett bra tillfälle för Yubico."*
